verses.pali: “Kismiṁ nu kho, bhikkhave, sati, kiṁ upādāya, kiṁ abhinivissa:
verses.english: “Mendicants, when what exists, because of grasping what and insisting on what,

verses.pali: ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassatī”ti?
verses.english: does someone regard things like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
“Our teachings are rooted in the Buddha. …”

verses.pali: “rūpe kho, bhikkhave, sati, rūpaṁ upādāya, rūpaṁ abhinivissa …pe…
verses.english: “When form exists, because of grasping form and insisting on form …

verses.pali: viññāṇe sati, viññāṇaṁ upādāya, viññāṇaṁ abhinivissa:
verses.english: When consciousness exists, because of grasping consciousness and insisting on consciousness,

verses.pali: ‘etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attā’ti samanupassati.
verses.english: someone regards it like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self.’

verses.pali: vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, api nu taṁ anupādāya etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attāti samanupasseyyāti?
verses.english: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would you regard it like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”

verses.pali: vipariṇāmadhammaṁ, api nu taṁ anupādāya etaṁ mama, esohamasmi, eso me attāti samanupasseyyāti?
verses.english: “But by not grasping what’s impermanent, suffering, and perishable, would you regard it like this: ‘This is mine, I am this, this is my self’?”
They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’”
